newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - U.S. technology trade publications.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - U.S. technology trade publications.

text.p: For the week of Feb. 17, here are some of the top stories reported in major U.S. technology trade publications.

NETWORK WORLD - U.S. Robotics Corp's product strategy to deliver higher-speed modems includes a planned dual-mode modem capable of delivering both 56 kbs and asymmetric digital subscriber line transmissions of up to six megabits per second, Network World reported in its Feb. 17 issue. Initial products for the system, called V.Everything, would become available in mid-1998 and priced around $200, the article said.

PC WEEK - The next round of Internet browser software upgrades from Microsoft Corp and Netscape Communications Corp will embed software formats needed to let Web sites or intranet servers become desktop "channels" that can deliver content automatically without the need of third-party "push" technology, PC Week said Feb. 17.

Bay Networks Inc is readying new technology that will greatly speed Internet protocol processing, PC Week reported Feb. 17. The company will introduce next week Switch Node, a network layer 3 switch that boosts the performance of IP-based and IPX networks. market, CRW reported Feb. 17.

COMPUTERWORLD - A new generation of "push" technology software could help sales representatives find new prospects, alert field offices to sudden prices changes and even make it easier for information system managers to distribute software, but the technology is still immature, Computerworld reported Feb. 17.
COMPUTER RESELLER NEWS - Microsoft will go head to head this week with router hardware vendors, making public its plans to integrate Internet software routing technology into
its Windows NT software, CRN reported Feb. 17. Microsoft is laying the groundwork for NT to act as the backbone of a virtual private network, or extranet, one source told CRN.

Intel Corp will position the Pentium II chip, code-named Klamath, as a high-end corporate desktop and workstation processor, while keeping the Pentium Pro as the processor of choice for enterprise servers. The Pentium II is scheduled to ship in May, starting at $750, CRN reported.
INTERACTIVE WEEK - Marimba Inc is planning a slew of

announcements for later this month, designed to bolster its image among corporations, as it aims its technology for transmitting digital data to desktop and portable computers to business users, Interactive Week reported Feb. 17.
The Internet Service Provider industry still remains a money-losing pit, based on the year-end financials of the leading publicly traded Internet access providers, Interactive Week reported Feb. 17.
INFOWORLD - Microsoft plans to announce specifications in April for a device bay that will allow hardware upgrades to
the forthcoming NetPC, in effect reopening a sealed box, InfoWorld reported Feb. 17.
Sybase Inc plans in April to unveil a new version of its Sybase IQ data mart server as part of a strategy to better integrate its product lines, InfoWorld reported.

INFORMATION WEEK - Massachusetts has been contacted by officials of the Texas attorney general's office about joining a state antitrust investigation of Microsoft's Internet software practices, Information Week reported Feb. 17.
Microsoft is extending its Windows CE operating system while Sun Microsystems Inc is planning a Java operating system as a new battle heats up over thin clients, Information Week reported.

EE TIMES - Intel will kick off its planned sales shift from processors to processor modules Monday when it rolls out its Mobile Module for notebook computers, a PC-sized board that integrates a P55C-class Pentium chip, core system logic chip and other technologies, EE Times reported Feb. 17.

Automotive electronics makers are working frantically to resolve the highly publicized safety problems with auto airbags, which pose a threat to children and small adults involved in collisions. Smart sensors are on the drawing board to determine a passenger's size before triggering the airbag, EE Times reported Feb. 17.
ELECTRONIC BUYERS' NEWS - As Taiwan furiously ramps up in DRAM chips, some Taiwanese companies plan to make waves in another market, flash memory, with comapnies like Macronix
International Co Ltd, Winbond Electronics Corp and others bringing out devices and expanding products, EBN reported Feb. 17.
Having undergone numerous trial developments in 1996, cable modems are poised to begin making commercial headway, but many obstacles to the technology's adoption persist, EE Times reported Feb. 17.

COMPUTER RETAIL WEEK - Intel will delay consumer marketing of its next generation microprocessor, code-named Klamath, until the second half of the year, months after the chip is available to business PC users, CRW reported Feb. 17.

Direct Broadcast Satellite set-top boxes that can control a DVD player or faciliate Internet access are on the horizon as DBS manufacturers set their sites on the massive U.S. cable market, CRW reported Feb. 17.
